rows.grounds: Fused sequence: tatra-sthāḥ (staying there) + muni-patnyaḥ (sages' wives) + mām (me) + dṛṣṭvā (having seen) + sa-ādaram-akṣamāḥ (with respect, unable to endure); sandhi and compounding preserved as given.
rows.morph: fused: tatra-stha.nom.pl.f + muni-patnī.nom.pl.f + asmad.acc.sg + dṛś.abs + sa-ādara-akṣama.nom.pl.f

items.question: What reaction did the sage-wives staying there have upon seeing the speaker?
premises: The sage-wives were present in that place.
Upon seeing the speaker, they became respectful yet unable to endure.
items.inference: The sight of the speaker provoked in the sage-wives a response marked by both respect and intolerance.
uncertainties: The precise nuance of akṣamāḥ (impatient, unable to bear, or overcome) depends on the following context.
items.plain_english: The sage-wives who were there saw me and, though respectful, could not contain themselves.
